note: Capabilities with no caller outside scripts/. See scripts/check-callers.ts and #72. This file may only SHRINK — the check fails when an entry becomes reachable and is not removed. 40 on 2026-09-16; app.mcp_expire_codes wired the same day; the three hq_*_tool wrappers, app.expire_temporary_staff and app.expire_undo_offers wired the same day under #272; app.autonomy_for wired by 0421 under #15 — the dial now decides something; public.project_artifacts wired as an hq-api section under #260. 0451 dropped public.hq_stranded_work and public.hq_eval_latest: the Governance page now reads both through app.hq_governance, so the separate wrappers were a second door to the same data. 31 -> 29 on 2026-09-17. 0452 dropped public.what_i_can_do (a second implementation of capabilityBrief, which builds every prompt) and public.hq_output_shapes (a mouth over a registry nothing reads); public.containers_stored_as_documents gained its caller in check:leaks. 29 -> 26 on 2026-09-17. check:callers learned that an OPERATOR COMMAND is a caller — a script an npm script runs, excluding verify:*, poc:* and the gate. Eight entries were reachable by a documented command Grant runs (eval, check:leaks, purge:fixtures, telegram:bots, inventory, slack:backfill) and were never dead. 26 -> 18 on 2026-09-17. 0454/0455 dropped the superseded task API: app.task_add is the live one the gateway and the Tasks tab use. Dropping the three wrappers PROVED app.project_tasks and app.set_task_state dead, which is why the wrappers went first. 18 -> 15 on 2026-09-17. 2026-09-17: app.needs_me_pressure removed — the morning briefing now says how many requests the needs_me cap is holding back and how long the oldest has waited (0469). Both were things nothing said: the cap hid the sixth request silently, and "past a real deadline" cannot see a request nobody dated. 15 -> 14. 2026-09-17: app.channel_for and app.slack_channels_for_project REMOVED (0470) — both read slack_channel_map and src/slack/provision.ts queries that table directly in six places for the columns each step needs, so the provisioner outgrew them. Wiring six working queries to call them would be the mechanical connection #272 forbids. 14 -> 12. public.awaiting_review wired as the `review` section under #276 — 0471 made it able to return a row at all. public.raise_proposals wired by the proposal-round duty under #49/#272 — 0473: nothing had ever turned an impediment into a proposal. 2026-09-18: app.proposals_sent and public.proposals_to_send left the baseline because the proposal round now calls them (0489). They were not dead code — they were #49's loop with its last link missing, so the office raised proposals correctly and never told Grant. That is what this check is for: the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. 2026-09-18, second pass: all eight survivors now carry a reason in `why`, which is what #272 asks for — the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. One of the eight, `app.suppress_delivery`, is the interesting answer: it is unreachable because the state it acts on never occurs, not because a caller was forgotten. An entry with no reason remains an admission rather than a decision.

why.app.create_temporary_specialist: FOR THE OFFICE, not for Grant. It is the only route by which the application role may add staff, and #128's hand-off is what uses it when a job needs a specialist the roster has not got. Only `verify:agents` names it today because no real job has yet needed one — the absence is a fact about traffic, not a missing caller, and a button for it would be Grant hiring somebody to answer a question he has not asked.
why.app.notification_patterns: A READER THAT WRITES NOTHING, and says so in its own comment: candidate patterns for what the office might learn about when to interrupt him. `npm run levels` and the learning page answer the question a person actually asks; this is the raw shape behind them.
why.app.suppress_delivery: THE ARCHITECTURE DOES NOT HAVE THE WINDOW IT NEEDS. It stops a QUEUED message going out when an undo lands first. `public.deliveries` has only ever held `sent` and `failed` — the notifier writes the row at the moment it sends, so there is no interval in which a pending delivery exists to be suppressed. Reachable the day delivery becomes a queue; inventing a caller before then would be a control for a state that cannot occur.
why.app.task_delete_pushed: #259 Phase 1: the provider seam, built before the provider it exists for. The Issue asks for Vikunja behind an abstraction and for the task domain to be ready for one WITHOUT requiring it, so these five RPCs ship ahead of their caller by design rather than by oversight. The caller is the Vikunja provider; the moment it exists these entries go stale and this check fails until they are removed, which is the property that makes this a baseline and not an allowlist. verify:mytasks drives all five as a fake provider, which is what proves the seam is provider-neutral.
